justification: The second GRPO layer is trained to identify and correct errors in the first layer's response, i.e. the revision step; evidence is lab gains on math reasoning benchmarks, no deployment.
Object is self-modification of an inappropriate output given feedback (moral self-correction); the scale hypothesis is tested by prompting experiments across model sizes in the lab.
Studies multi-round intrinsic self-correction and explains its performance convergence; lab experiments plus mechanistic analysis, never a practice setting.
Headline artefact is Self-Correction Bench, a controlled instrument separating activation failure from capability; used to measure 14 open models in the lab.
Contribution is the Step CoT Check format and fine-tuning that produce the judgement on a reasoning path, including locating the wrong step; validated on multiple benchmarks in the lab.
ISC with Partial Answer Masking fine-tunes models to rewrite their own initial output in a self-triggered way; lab experiments on commonsense and factual reasoning tasks.
Novelty is the feedback design, multi-aspect critiques and scoring with intent clarification, that drives the rewrite; conditions compared against baselines in lab experiments.
Formalises self-correction as a closed-loop controller emitting targeted repair instructions (runner-up: the Convergence Judge, termination control); validated on the authors' bench, lab only.
Asks whether feedback-driven moral self-correction works at all, via behavioural and hidden-state analysis of the correction step; lab study, no practice setting.
Systematically compares iterative refinement dynamics in open-ended generation versus multiple choice across scales and families; lab experiments on NLU and reasoning tasks.
The If-or-Else prompt makes the model assess its own confidence before it may correct, so the mechanism is the judgement; evidence is lab experiments against the initial answers.
STaSC iteratively fine-tunes the model on solely self-generated correction data, an outer loop changing the agent between rounds; validated on a QA task in the lab.
Contribution is the feedback content, emotional cues injected once a verifier flags a response, that triggers the revised answer; lab benchmarks on safety, hallucination and reasoning.
CoCoS designs multi-turn rewards so small models progressively correct their own code across turns; validated on MBPP and HumanEval in the lab.
SFS-DPO trains the correction that follows step-level self-verification, with analysis of self-correction frequency; in-domain and out-of-domain lab evaluations only.
An evolutionary outer loop rewrites the prompt across generations so the model acquires new strategies; validated on MathVista, M3CoT and GeoBench-VLM subtasks in the lab.
Tests whether supervised synthetic error injection can induce the correct-your-own-error step and reports failure; lab experiments contrasting synthetic with on-policy errors.
Adds a metacognitive monitor producing difficulty and confidence judgements that gate whether reasoning proceeds; the paper states it presents no empirical validation, only a framework.
LoT's novelty is a symbolic-logic (Reductio ad Absurdum) check verifying each reasoning step before it stands; validated across arithmetic, commonsense, symbolic and causal tasks.
Contributes a debate-based measurement procedure for whether a model holds its answer under critique, an instrument beyond one mechanism; run over existing reasoning benchmarks.
Audits self-critique versus sound external verification as the acceptance check in Game of 24, Graph Coloring and STRIPS; a lab study varying the verifier condition.
A cyclic questioning-reflection-calibration loop turns internal feedback into a rewritten reasoning chain; validated on open reasoning datasets with sensitivity studies, lab only.
Claim is that the hierarchical arrangement of agents beats single-agent and stochastic baselines in search efficiency; prototype MASTER run on two simulation campaigns by the authors.
Detected parse errors are fed back with retrieved grammar rules so the LLM rewrites its output, the correction being the contribution; validated on three datasets in the lab.
LR2Bench is the instrument: 850 constraint-satisfaction samples for measuring long-chain reflective reasoning, used to evaluate existing LLMs and LRMs in the lab.
